name: Κατακόμβες Μήλου
taglineEn: One of the most significant early Christian monuments in Greece
description: Carved into the volcanic rock of Tripiti, the Catacombs of Milos date from the 1st to 5th century AD. With over 8,000 burials in 291 tombs, they are among the largest Christian catacombs in the Mediterranean and the only ones in Greece.

name: Αρχαίο Θέατρο Μήλου
taglineEn: Hellenistic theater overlooking the Gulf of Milos
description: Built in the Hellenistic period, this remarkably preserved theater sits on the hillside of Tripiti with sweeping views of the Gulf of Milos. A short walk away is the exact spot where the Venus de Milo statue was discovered by a farmer in 1820.

name: Κάστρο Πλάκας
taglineEn: Medieval fortress with the best sunset on the island
description: Perched at the highest point of Plaka, the Kastro dates from the 13th-century Venetian occupation. Its whitewashed alleys and the tiny Church of Panagia Thalassitra crown the hilltop. The views from the top — island-wide, 360° — are the most spectacular on Milos.

name: Αρχαιολογικό Μουσείο
taglineEn: Home to a replica of the Venus de Milo
description: Located in Plaka, this museum houses artifacts spanning the Neolithic era through the Roman period. The centerpiece is a plaster cast of the Venus de Milo, alongside remarkable finds from ancient Filakopi and other sites across the island.

name: Μουσείο Μεταλλείων Μήλου
taglineEn: 8,000 years of mining history on a volcanic island
description: Milos has been mined since antiquity for obsidian, bentonite and perlite. The Mining Museum in Adamas tells this remarkable 8,000-year story through exhibits, minerals, tools and scale models — a must for geology and history enthusiasts.

name: Σαρακήνικο
taglineEn: The iconic lunar landscape — Milos' most photographed sight
description: Formed by volcanic ash shaped over millennia by wind and waves, Sarakiniko's brilliant white pumice formations create an otherworldly moonscape unlike anything else in Greece. Popular for swimming, cliff jumping and watching the sun set over the Aegean.

name: Παπάφραγκας
taglineEn: Secret sea caves carved into volcanic cliffs
description: Three narrow sea inlets carved into white volcanic rock form natural swimming pools with crystal-clear turquoise water. Steps cut into the cliff lead down to the water. Nearby lie the ruins of ancient Filakopi, one of the oldest Bronze Age settlements in the Aegean.

name: Συρμάτα Κλήμα
taglineEn: The most colourful traditional fishing village in the Cyclades
description: Klima's syrmata are two-storey boathouses built directly into the volcanic rock: ground floor for the fishing boat, upper floor for the family. Painted in vivid reds, blues and ochres, these unique structures are found only on Milos and are among the most photographed subjects in the Cyclades.

name: Αρχαία Φυλακωπή
taglineEn: One of the most important Bronze Age cities in the Aegean
description: Occupied from around 2300 to 1100 BC, Filakopi was a leading Aegean city of the early Bronze Age, powered by Milos' abundant obsidian — the steel of the ancient world. Partially excavated by the British School at Athens, the site sits on the northeastern coast and is open to visitors.

name: Τόπος Ανακάλυψης Αφροδίτης
taglineEn: Where the world's most famous sculpture was found in 1820
description: In February 1820, a farmer named Yorgos Kentrotas unearthed the Venus de Milo in an ancient niche on his land near Tripiti. The statue — now in the Louvre — left Milos the same year, but a small monument marks the exact spot where one of history's greatest sculptures lay buried for centuries.
